safi-cedvel:1-2.t:
* I'rab:
(باسم) is attached to a ḥāl from the agent of اقرأ, i.e. "clothed in the name" or "beginning with the name".. (الذي) is a relative in the position of genitive, a naʿt of ربّك (من علق) is attached to the second (خلق).
Clause: «اقرأ ... » has no grammatical position; it is an opening clause.
And the clause: «خلق (الأولى) » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
And the clause: «خلق (الثانية) » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption [Note: or a badal of the ṣila clause, if the object of "created" is taken to be (كلّ شيء) and then specified with the creation of man.].

* Benefits:
- The beginning of the revelation:
Most commentators said: This sūra is the first sūra of the noble Qur'an to be revealed, and the first revealed were five verses from its beginning, up to His saying (ما لَمْ يَعْلَمْ). On the authority of ʿĀʾisha, Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The first thing with which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was begun, of the revelation, was the good vision — (and in Muslim:) the true vision in sleep — and he never saw a vision but it came like the break of dawn. Then solitude was made beloved to him, and he used to be alone in the cave of Ḥirāʾ, engaging in taḥannuth there (which is worship for a number of nights) before returning to his family, and he would take provisions for that; then he would return to Khadīja and take provisions for a like period, until the revelation came to him.
In one report: The truth came upon him suddenly while he was in the cave of Ḥirāʾ, and the angel came to him and said: "Read." He said: "I am not a reader." He said: "He took me and pressed me until I could bear no more, then released me and said: 'Read.' I said: 'I am not a reader.' He took me and pressed me a second time until I could bear no more, then released me and said: 'Read.' I said: 'I am not a reader.' He took me and pressed me a third time until I could bear no more, then released me and said: (اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ. خَلَقَ الْإِنْسانَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ. اقْرَأْ وَرَبُّكَ الْأَكْرَمُ. الَّذِي عَلَّمَ بِالْقَلَمِ. عَلَّمَ الْإِنْسانَ ما لَمْ يَعْلَمْ)." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned with it, his shoulder muscles trembling, until he entered upon Khadīja and said: "Cover me, cover me." They covered him until the fear left him. Then he said to Khadīja: "O Khadīja, what is the matter with me?" and told her the news, and said: "I fear for myself."
Khadīja said to him: "Never! Rejoice, for by Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. You maintain the ties of kinship, you speak the truth, you bear burdens, you earn for the destitute, you honour the guest, and you help in the calamities of truth." Then Khadīja went with him until she brought him to Waraqa ibn Nawfal, who was Khadīja's cousin; he was a man who had become Christian in the Jāhiliyya and used to write the Hebrew scripture, writing from the Gospel in Hebrew as much as Allah willed him to write; he was an old man who had gone blind. Khadīja said to him: "O my cousin, listen to your nephew." Waraqa said to him: "O my nephew, what do you see?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ told him what he had seen, and Waraqa said to him: "This is the Nāmūs which Allah sent down upon Moses. Would that I were a young man in it, when your people expel you." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Will they expel me?" He said: "Yes. No man has ever come with what you have come with but was met with hostility, and if your day reaches me while I am alive, I shall support you with strong support." Then Waraqa did not delay long before he died, and the revelation paused. Al-Bukhārī added: He said: The revelation paused for a time, so that the Prophet ﷺ — as has reached us — grieved with a grief by which he went out several times to throw himself from the tops of high mountains; and whenever he reached the summit of a mountain, Gabriel appeared to him and said: "O Muhammad, you are truly the Messenger of Allah," whereupon his heart was calmed and his eye was comforted and he returned. And when the pause of the revelation grew long upon him he went out for the like of that, and Gabriel said the same to him.

safi-cedvel:3-5.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is circumstantial (الذي) is in the position of nominative, a naʿt of الأكرم [Note: it is possible that it is a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ ربّك.. or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو" (he), and the clause is an explanatory resumption.], (بالقلم) is attached to (علّم) and (الباء) denotes instrumentality [Note: it is possible to attach the prepositional phrase to the implied second object, i.e. "taught man writing with the pen".].
Clause: «اقرأ ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive, for emphasis.
And the clause: «ربّك الأكرم» is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from the agent of اقرأ.
And the clause: «علّم بالقلم» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
And the clause: «علّم الإنسان» has no grammatical position; it is a badal of (علّم بالقلم).
And the clause: «لم يعلم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (ما) [Note: or in the position of accusative, a naʿt of the indefinite qualified (ما).].

* Morphology:
(3) الأكرم: it has the form of the elative, pattern أفعل, but in meaning it is an intensification of generosity, i.e. His generosity exceeds all generosity.

safi-cedvel:6-7.t:
* I'rab:
(كلّا) is a particle of deterrence and rebuke [Note: and it is for alerting according to some, and in the sense of "truly" (ḥaqqan) according to others.], (اللام) is the shifted lām, for emphasis, (أن) is a maṣdar particle, and the pronoun in (رآه) refers to الإنسان, i.e. he saw himself.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن رآه..) is in the position of genitive by an omitted lām, attached to (يطغى), i.e. "because he sees himself self-sufficient".
Clause: «إنّ الإنسان ليطغى ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «يطغى ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of inna.
And the clause: «رآه ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
And the clause: «استغنى» is in the position of accusative, a second mafʿūl bihi of the seeing of the heart.

* Morphology:
(7) رآه: the madda in it is from a hamza and a quiescent alif, which are the ʿayn and lām of the word; when the pronoun of the third person came, the two alifs were assimilated and the madda was placed above them because of the accidental medial position; the original is رأى.

safi-cedvel:8-8.t:
* I'rab:
(إلى ربّك) is attached to the khabar of inna (الرجعى) is the ism of inna, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the implied fatḥa on the alif.
Clause: «إنّ إلى ربّك الرجعى ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(الرجعى): a samāʿī maṣdar (reported usage) of the triliteral رجع; its pattern is فعلى, with ḍamma then sukūn.. There are also الرجوع and المرجع, with kasra on the jīm.

safi-cedvel:9-10.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for the interrogative of astonishment [Note: and that is in the three following places, and (أرأيت) is in the sense of "tell me", and the second object is omitted, indicated by the following clause ألم يعلم.., and the seeing may be visual, in which case there is no interpretation needed.], (عبدا) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative, its governing verb being ينهى (إذا) is an adverbial stripped of the conditional sense, in the position of accusative, attached to (ينهى) ..
Clause: «أرأيت ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «ينهى ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
And the clause: «صلّى» is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.

safi-cedvel:11-12.t:
* I'rab:
(كان) is a defective past verb in the position of jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) (على الهدى) is attached to the khabar of كان (أو) is for conjunction (بالتقوى) is attached to (أمر)
Clause: «أرأيت ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «إن كان على الهدى ... » has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical.
And the clause: «أمر» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كان.. and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the preceding sense of astonishment, or the sense of interrogation in His saying: ألم يعلم بأنّ الله يرى ...

safi-cedvel:13-14.t:
* I'rab:
The object of (رأيت) is omitted, indicated by (الذي ينهى..) [Note: in verse (9) of the sūra.],
(كذّب) is in the position of jussive, the protasis, and likewise (تولّى), (الهمزة) is for the interrogative of reproach..
And the interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله يرى) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (يعلم).
Clause: «أرأيت ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive [Note: al-Zamakhsharī parsed the preceding verses in another way, which we summarize in what follows, quoting from al-Jumal:
"The first أرأيت has as its first object the relative, and the second (رأيت) is redundant, for emphasis; the clause of the condition and its answer, within the sphere of the second, is the second object of the first (رأيت); and the first object of the third (رأيت) is omitted, its implied form being 'have you seen him', and the clause of the second condition and its answer — which is the interrogative clause ألم يعلم.. — is the second object of the third (رأيت).. And that is sound just as it is sound in your saying: 'If I honour you, will you honour me?'" End of quotation.].
And the clause: «كذّب ... » has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical.
And the clause: «تولّى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كذّب.
And the clause: «ألم يعلم ... » is in the position of accusative, a second mafʿūl bihi of the verb of seeing.
And the clause: «يرى ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of أنّ.. and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the second object, i.e.: "if he denied and turned away, does this forbidder know that Allah sees him?"

safi-cedvel:15-18.t:
* I'rab:
(كلّا) is a particle of deterrence and rebuke (اللام) is the preparatory lām for the oath (إن) is a jussive-governing conditional particle (اللام) is the lām of oath (نسفعن) is an imperfect verb indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of nominative, and (النون) is the light nūn of emphasis (بالناصية) is attached to (نسفعن), and (الباء) denotes instrumentality (ناصية) is a badal of the definite الناصية (الفاء) is the connecting particle of the jawāb of an implied condition (اللام) is the lām of command (السين) denotes the future (ندع) is an imperfect, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the implied ḍamma on the wāw omitted in writing to suit the connected reading; the agent is "we", for glorification.
Clause: «إن لم ينته ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «نسفعن ... » has no grammatical position; it is the jawāb al-qasam.. and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath.
And the clause: «ليدع ... » is in the position of jussive, the answer to an implied condition, i.e.: "if he is able to ward off the punishment, let him call his council."
And the clause: «سندع الزبانية ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.

* Morphology:
(15) ينته: an ʿilāl by omission to suit the jussive; its origin is ينتهي; its pattern is يفتع.
(17) ناديه: the name of the gathering place in which the people assemble; its pattern is فاعل.
(18) سندع: the weak letter — the lām of the verb — was dropped from the muṣḥaf orthography because of the connected reading.
(الزبانية): plural of زبنية, with kasra on the first, sukūn on the second, kasra on the third and a light yāʾ; it is from الزبن, i.e. pushing; or it is the plural of زبنيّ in the relative form, whose origin is زبانيّ with a doubled yāʾ, then the tāʾ came as a substitute for the yāʾ.. It is stated in al-Qāmūs: الزبنية (like هبرية) is a rebellious one of the jinn and humans, a violent one, or a policeman; its plural is زبانية, or its singular is زبنيّ.

* Rhetoric:
Figurative attribution: in His saying, the Exalted «ناصِيَةٍ كاذِبَةٍ خاطِئَةٍ».
Here the forelock is described with what is mentioned, although it is a description of its owner, by way of exaggeration, since it indicates his being described as lying and sinning a fortiori, and indicates that, due to the intensity of his lying and sinning, it is as if every part of him lies and sins. It is like His saying, the Exalted: «تَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُهُمُ الْكَذِبَ» and their saying: "Her face describes beauty." The attribution is figurative, being the attribution of what belongs to the whole to the part.
Free metonymy (al-majāz al-mursal): in His saying, the Exalted «فَلْيَدْعُ نادِيَهُ».
That is: let him call the people of the council; for the council is not called, only its people are called, so the place was named and the occupant intended. The majāz is mursal, its relation being locality (maḥalliyya). Al-nādī is the gathering place in which the people converse, i.e. gather for talk.

safi-cedvel:19-19.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) is a prohibitive, jussive-governing particle (الواو) is a conjunction in both places..
Clause: «لا تطعه ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «اسجد ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause: «اقترب ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.

* Morphology:
(تطعه): it contains an ʿilāl by omission to suit the jussive; its origin is تطيعه in the nominative; when it was made jussive, the ʿayn was made quiescent and two quiescent letters met, the yāʾ and the ʿayn, so the yāʾ was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents; its pattern is تفله.
